subject: religious-studies
source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel GCSE Religious Studies A (1RA0) specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Area of Study 1: Study of Religion
units.blurb: One religion in depth: beliefs, practices, sources and expression

units.name: Area of Study 2: Second Religion & Philosophy/Ethics
units.blurb: A second religion plus philosophy and ethics (or textual studies)

topics.name: Beliefs & Teachings
topics.blurb: Core beliefs and teachings of the chosen religion

topics.name: Sources of Wisdom & Authority
topics.blurb: Scriptures and authorities the religion draws on

topics.name: Forms of Expression & Ways of Life
topics.blurb: How belief is expressed in life, art and community

topics.name: Second Religion: Beliefs & Teachings
topics.blurb: Core beliefs of the second religion studied

topics.name: Second Religion: Practices
topics.blurb: Worship and practices of the second religion

topics.name: Arguments for the Existence of God
topics.blurb: Design, causation, miracles and religious experience

topics.name: Relationships & Families in the 21st Century
topics.blurb: Religious teachings on marriage, family and relationships

topics.name: Textual Studies (alternative)
topics.blurb: Study of Mark's Gospel or the Qur'an

connections.why: Beliefs are expressed and enacted through religious practices and worship
Beliefs are grounded in and justified by the religion's sources of authority
Sacred sources prescribe how worship and festivals are carried out
Beliefs shape how a faith is expressed in daily life, art and community
Shared practices are a major way religious identity is expressed
Studying the first religion's beliefs gives a comparative basis for the second
Comparing practices across two religions highlights similarities and differences
The second religion's practices flow from its beliefs, as with the first
Beliefs about God connect directly to philosophical arguments for God's existence
Scriptural teaching is the basis for religious views on relationships and families
Core beliefs shape ethical teaching on marriage and the family
Textual study examines in depth the kind of sources of authority met in Area of Study 1
A second perspective on God enriches the philosophical debate about existence
Both apply structured argument and evaluation to questions of religion and ethics
